standard_prerequisites.name: The stable module (B,a,b) attached to a point of the moduli space, the simple module S_i concentrated at a vertex i of I^0, and the maps alpha_i and beta_i of the complex built from B, a, b
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the same subsection; the author displays the complex explicitly before the counted statement (source lines 1700-1708)
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the two maps whose injectivity and surjectivity the statement is about, and the modules between which the homomorphisms in the proof are taken.

standard_prerequisites.name: The theta-functional of the subgraph I^0 and the fact that both the simple module S_i and the stable module have theta equal to zero
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof at source lines 1727-1730
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes every non-zero homomorphism between the two stable modules an isomorphism, which is the mechanism of the proof.

core_obligations: The kernel argument: the kernel of alpha_i gives a homomorphism from the simple module S_i to the stable module (B,a,b) (proof lines 1725-1728).

The dichotomy: both modules are zeta^bullet-stable and have the same theta-functional value, namely zero, so that homomorphism is either zero or an isomorphism; hence alpha_i is injective unless the module is the simple one (proof lines 1728-1731).

The dual argument for beta: the cokernel of beta_i is the dual of the space of homomorphisms from the stable module to S_i, so the same reasoning gives the surjectivity of beta_i (proof lines 1731-1732).

The two alternatives of the statement: either W = 0, in which case the module is the simple module S_i, or both alpha_i injective and beta_i surjective (statement lines 1713-1720, concluded at proof line 1732).
proof_roadmap: 把 alpha_i 的核解释为从单模 S_i 到稳定模 (B,a,b) 的一个同态。
两者都 zeta^bullet-稳定且 theta 值同为 0，故该同态非零即为同构，于是 alpha_i 单；再把 beta_i 的余核解释为反方向同态空间的对偶，同样论证给出 beta_i 满。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the dichotomy for a zeta-stable module at a vertex of the subgraph I^0 (author Lemma at source lines 1710-1720, label lem:betasurj): either the module is the simple module concentrated at that vertex, or the two maps of the complex are injective and surjective respectively. The proof (source lines 1724-1732) is a standard-argument one but with a real mechanism: it reads the kernel of alpha_i as a homomorphism from the simple module S_i to the stable module and then uses that both are zeta^bullet-stable with the same theta-functional value to conclude that a non-zero such homomorphism is an isomorphism (proof lines 1728-1731), and it obtains the surjectivity of beta_i by identifying its cokernel with the dual of the space of homomorphisms in the other direction (proof lines 1731-1732). The lemma is the technical input for the author's description of the strata, and the author notes just before the proof that it completes the proof of the preceding proposition. H2.
